title: 4. Economy:RRB + SSC CGL + DSSSB Combined Economy Mock Test

questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was established in which year?
The Reserve Bank of India was nationalized in which year?
Where is the headquarters of the Reserve Bank of India located?
Who was the first Governor of the Reserve Bank of India?
The RBI acts as the banker to which of the following?
options: The Government of India and state governments

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a function of the RBI?
The repo rate refers to which of the following?
options: The rate at which RBI lends money to commercial banks
The rate at which commercial banks lend to the public
The rate of interest on savings accounts
The rate at which RBI borrows from the government

questions.q: The reverse repo rate refers to which of the following?
options: The rate at which RBI borrows money from commercial banks
The rate at which banks lend to businesses
The rate at which the government borrows from RBI
The interest rate on fixed deposits

questions.q: An increase in the repo rate generally leads to which of the following?
options: Costlier loans and lower inflation (contractionary effect)

questions.q: The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) refers to which of the following?
options: The percentage of deposits banks must keep as cash with RBI
The percentage of profit banks must declare as dividend
The ratio of loans to deposits in a bank
The minimum capital a bank must maintain

questions.q: The Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) refers to which of the following?
options: The reserve banks must maintain in the form of cash, gold or approved securities
The rate of interest on government bonds
The minimum wage banks must pay employees
The percentage of foreign investment allowed in banks

questions.q: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the RBI primarily decides on which of the following?
The Monetary Policy Committee of RBI consists of how many members?
The RBI's inflation targeting framework primarily aims to keep retail inflation (CPI) within which broad range?
The Bank Rate, as used by RBI, refers to which of the following?
options: The rate at which RBI lends to banks without any collateral for long-term purposes
The rate at which the government taxes banks
The interest rate on savings accounts
The rate of GST charged on banking services

questions.q: Open Market Operations (OMO) conducted by RBI refer to which of the following?
options: Buying and selling of government securities to regulate money supply

questions.q: Which of the following banks is known as the 'lender of last resort'?
NABARD, which focuses on rural and agricultural credit, was established in which year?
NABARD stands for which of the following?
options: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
National Bureau of Agricultural Research and Development
National Association for Banking and Rural Development
National Bank for Applied Research and Development

questions.q: Which institution regulates and supervises Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) in India?
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) primarily regulates which of the following?
The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) regulates which sector?
Bank nationalization in India first took place in which year?
How many banks were nationalized in the first phase of bank nationalization in 1969?
The second phase of bank nationalization took place in which year?
Which is the largest public sector bank in India by assets?
The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) is a subsidiary of which institution?
As per DICGC rules, deposits in a bank are insured up to what amount per depositor per bank?
Which committee's recommendations led to the establishment of Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) in India?
options: Narasimhan Working Group on Rural Banks

questions.q: Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) were established in which year?
The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) is known for developing which of the following?
Which of the following is a function of commercial banks but NOT of the central bank (RBI)?
options: Accepting deposits from the public and lending to them
Acting as banker to the government

questions.q: The term 'Marginal Standing Facility (MSF)' refers to which of the following?
options: A facility under which banks can borrow overnight funds from RBI against government securities

questions.q: Demonetisation of ₹500 and ₹1000 currency notes in India was carried out in which year?
The Basel Norms, which banks must comply with, primarily relate to which of the following?
options: Capital adequacy and risk management standards for banks

questions.q: Priority Sector Lending (PSL) by banks in India primarily focuses on providing credit to which of the following sectors?
options: Agriculture, MSMEs, education, housing and weaker sections

questions.q: Which body issues currency notes in India (other than the one-rupee note and coins)?
The one-rupee note and coins in India are issued by which authority?
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India

questions.q: Which of the following best describes 'Non-Performing Assets (NPAs)' in banking?
options: Loans on which interest or principal payment is overdue for a specified period
Assets that generate the highest profit for banks

questions.q: Which committee is associated with recommendations on banking sector reforms in India in the early 1990s?
GDP stands for which of the following?
Gross Domestic Product (GDP) measures which of the following?
options: The total value of goods and services produced within a country's borders in a given period
The total income earned by a country's citizens abroad
The total tax collected by the government
The total value of a country's exports only

questions.q: GNP stands for which of the following?
GNP differs from GDP mainly by including which of the following?
options: Net income earned by residents from abroad, minus income earned by non-residents domestically

questions.q: Which organization in India is responsible for calculating and releasing GDP data?
Per capita income is calculated by which of the following methods?
options: Dividing national income by total population

questions.q: The First Five-Year Plan of India was launched in which year?
The First Five-Year Plan of India primarily focused on which sector?
The Second Five-Year Plan, based on the Mahalanobis model, primarily emphasized which sector?
Which body was responsible for formulating India's Five-Year Plans before being replaced?
The Planning Commission of India was established in which year?
NITI Aayog, which replaced the Planning Commission, was established in which year?
NITI Aayog stands for which of the following?
options: National Institute of Trade and Industry

questions.q: Who serves as the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog?
Unlike the Planning Commission, NITI Aayog primarily functions as which of the following?
options: A policy think tank without fund allocation powers

questions.q: The Twelfth (12th) Five-Year Plan of India covered which period?
Which of the following best defines 'inflation'?
options: A sustained increase in the general price level of goods and services
A decrease in the value of exports
An increase in the exchange rate of currency

questions.q: 'Deflation' refers to which of the following?
options: A sustained decrease in the general price level
An increase in GDP growth rate

questions.q: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) is primarily used to measure which of the following?
The Wholesale Price Index (WPI) primarily measures price changes at which level?
'Fiscal deficit' refers to which of the following?
options: The excess of total government expenditure over total revenue (excluding borrowings)
The excess of exports over imports
The excess of savings over investment
The excess of tax revenue over expenditure

questions.q: 'Disinvestment' by the government generally refers to which of the following?
options: Selling government stakes in public sector enterprises

questions.q: Which sector, as per common classification, includes agriculture and allied activities?
The manufacturing and industrial sector is classified under which sector of the economy?
Banking, education, and healthcare services are classified under which sector of the economy?
'Mixed economy', as followed by India, refers to which of the following?
options: Coexistence of both public and private sector participation
An economy run entirely by the government
An economy with no government intervention
An economy based only on agriculture

questions.q: The Green Revolution in India, which boosted agricultural production, began primarily in which decade?
Economic liberalization, privatization, and globalization (LPG reforms) in India were introduced in which year?
Who was the Finance Minister of India during the 1991 economic reforms?
The Human Development Index (HDI), used to rank countries, is published by which organization?
The 'Finance Commission' of India is primarily concerned with which of the following?
options: Distribution of tax revenue between the Union and the States

questions.q: The Finance Commission is constituted by the President of India after every how many years?
GST (Goods and Services Tax) in India was implemented in which year?
GST replaced which of the following types of taxes primarily?
options: Multiple indirect taxes like VAT, excise duty, and service tax

questions.q: Which of the following best describes 'mixed economy planning' concepts adopted through Five-Year Plans in India?
options: A blend of socialist planning with private sector participation
Complete state ownership of all industries
Complete free-market capitalism with no planning
An economy based purely on foreign aid

questions.q: The Union Budget of India is presented in which house of Parliament first?
Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with the Union Budget (Annual Financial Statement)?
The Union Budget in India is typically presented on which date, as per the current practice?
The Indian financial year runs from which period?
Who presents the Union Budget in Parliament?
The practice of presenting a separate Railway Budget from the Union Budget was discontinued in which year?
The Economic Survey of India is typically released in Parliament in relation to the Union Budget at which time?
options: A day or two before the Union Budget
At the end of the financial year

questions.q: The Economic Survey of India is prepared under the guidance of which official?
The Economic Survey primarily serves which of the following purposes?
options: Reviews the performance of the economy over the past year and outlines future policy directions
Functions as a legally binding financial document
Replaces the need for the Union Budget

questions.q: The 'Vote on Account' in the Indian budgetary process refers to which of the following?
options: A provision allowing the government to withdraw funds for a short period before the full budget is passed
A permanent budget requiring no renewal

questions.q: The 'Interim Budget' is typically presented under which circumstance?
options: In an election year, before a new government takes charge
Only when the fiscal deficit is high

questions.q: Which of the following best describes 'revenue expenditure' in the Union Budget?
options: Expenditure that does not create assets or reduce liabilities, such as salaries and subsidies
Expenditure that always creates new assets

questions.q: 'Capital expenditure' in the Union Budget primarily refers to which of the following?
options: Spending that creates assets or reduces liabilities, such as infrastructure investment

questions.q: The term 'revenue deficit' refers to which of the following?
options: The excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts
The excess of capital expenditure over capital receipts
The excess of exports over imports
The excess of savings over investment

questions.q: The 'Consolidated Fund of India' includes which of the following?
options: All revenues received and loans raised by the government
Only funds collected from income tax
Only funds meant for defense spending

questions.q: The 'Contingency Fund of India' is used for which of the following purposes?
options: To meet unforeseen expenditure pending authorization by Parliament
To pay salaries of Members of Parliament
To pay for foreign trips of ministers

questions.q: Which committee of Parliament examines the Union Budget in detail after its presentation?
options: Standing Committees on Finance and related ministries

questions.q: The 'Finance Bill' presented along with the Union Budget primarily deals with which of the following?
options: Proposed changes in taxation for the coming financial year

questions.q: The term 'disinvestment target' as mentioned in the Union Budget refers to which of the following?
options: The government's planned revenue from selling stakes in public sector undertakings
The target for reducing income tax rates
The target for increasing import duties
The target for reducing the number of government employees

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the term 'fiscal policy'?
options: Government's policy relating to taxation and public expenditure
RBI's policy relating to interest rates and money supply
Policy relating to foreign exchange reserves only
Policy relating to import-export tariffs only

questions.q: 'Monetary policy', as distinguished from fiscal policy, is primarily formulated by which institution?
The 'Direct Tax Code', discussed in the context of Union Budgets, aims to simplify which of the following?
options: Direct taxes such as income tax and corporate tax

questions.q: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India primarily performs which of the following functions?
options: Audits the accounts of the Union and State governments

questions.q: The FRBM Act, relevant to Union Budget discipline, stands for which of the following?
options: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act
Foreign Reserve and Bank Management Act
Financial Regulation and Banking Monitoring Act
Fiscal Reform and Budget Modernization Act

questions.q: The FRBM Act was enacted in which year with the aim of ensuring fiscal discipline?
